detected_by: echo $RETRO_ACTOR in a fresh Bash call printed sd31-transcribe despite this cycle's own earlier 'export RETRO_ACTOR=sd33-r4-e5-finalize' (run in a prior, now-discarded shell state, since shell state does not persist between Bash tool calls)
impact: Every dispatched agent's Bash tool call is a fresh shell that re-sources ~/.bashrc, which sets (plain assignment, but export-flag-sticky from an earlier exported line) RETRO_ACTOR=sd31-transcribe -- a leftover from a prior SD-31 session. Any lane that runs scripts/retro.py or scripts/verify.sh without explicitly re-exporting RETRO_ACTOR inline in the SAME bash invocation gets its events silently misattributed to sd31-transcribe.jsonl instead of its own actor's log.
resolution: not fixed this cycle -- ~/.bashrc is outside this bundle's granted write scope; worked around by inlining 'export RETRO_ACTOR=...' in the same Bash invocation as every retro.py/verify.sh call this cycle. Named for an operator to clear the stale ~/.bashrc lines 135-137 directly.
